subject: Post-call: POC connectivity, success criteria & SDK integration plan
messages:
From: Anna Rivera <anna@quanticai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Cheng <oliver@quanticai.com>
Date: 2028-09-27T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + trial priorities

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from my side and a couple of asks so we can get the trial moving. High-level goals we confirmed: 

- Validate streaming latency for short-form chat (avg response < 250ms p50)
- Measure token cost for our 3k/day conversation workload and delta vs current provider
- Ensure tool-calling works for our lookup service (external product catalog)

Key success criteria we want to see in the POC:
1) End-to-end sample flow for chat -> tool call -> structured response (JSON)
2) Baseline latency and cost report after a 2-week run
3) Minimal infra changes on our side (we prefer SDK + WebSocket streaming)

Immediate asks:
- Can you share an integration checklist + expected timeline?
- Who from Redwood will own SDK handoff / day-to-day support?
- Any network/VPC requirements we should prepare for?

I'll attach our internal trial requirements doc in a follow-up. Looking to kick off the week of Oct 9 if that's realistic.

Thanks,
Anna
Head of ML Integrations
Quantic AI

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Rivera <anna@quanticai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Cheng <oliver@quanticai.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-27T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + trial priorities

Anna — thanks for the clear summary, good alignment across the call. Below is a concrete POC plan and the integration checklist you'll need to start. I've also attached a concise MOP and a network checklist for your infra team (redwood-poc-mop-v1.pdf, network-access-checklist.xlsx).

POC plan (owner / timeline / success gates)
- POC length: 2 weeks of steady traffic after basic integration (target kickoff: 2028-10-10) — Owner: Ben Carter (Redwood) / Oliver (Quantic)
- Week 0 (prep): NDA + account creation, token provisioning, network whitelists, provide sample dataset (target: 3 business days)
- Week 1 (integration): SDK install, wire chat -> tool call paths, sample replay for baseline metrics (deliverable: end-to-end demo)
- Week 2 (run & collect): 48–72 hour steady-state run + analysis; deliver cost/latency report and sample structured outputs

Success criteria (concrete)
1) Functional: end-to-end chat flow with tool-calling returns correct JSON in >= 95% of test cases
2) Latency: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms for targeted 1–2k concurrent short sessions
3) Cost: tokens/unit within 20% of Redwood's published trial estimate (we'll provide a breakdown)
4) Reliability: no >5% error rate on tool-calls during steady-state run

Integration checklist (high level)
- Provide a staging API key and create trial account (Redwood)
- Network: allow outbound TLS to api.redwood.ai (standard ports) and open websocket traffic for streaming endpoints
- SDK: add redwood-js (v2.1+) or redwood-py (v1.8+) to your service; sample code provided in MOP
- Endpoints: text.generate (batch), chat.stream (websocket), function-calls via chat.generate payloads
- Data: sample dataset (CSV/JSON) and tool endpoints (catalog lookup) by Oct 4 to avoid prep delays

Ownership & support
- Primary Redwood contact (technical): Ben Carter — ben_carter@redwood.ai
- Account lead: Kimberly Park — kimberly_park@redwood.ai
- Escalations / SLA questions: Marissa Cole (cc'd)

Next steps
1) Quantic: confirm kickoff week and provide sample dataset + security contact (send network firewall IPs)
2) Redwood: share trial account + MOP (attached) and open a HubSpot deal + shared Drive with runbook
3) Schedule a 30-minute integration walkthrough (we propose Oct 11, 10:00 PT)

Let me know if you want the SDK snippets sent as a GitHub gist or pasted into the thread.

Thanks — K

Attachments: redwood-poc-mop-v1.pdf; network-access-checklist.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Rivera <anna@quanticai.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-28T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + trial priorities

Adding a few technical specifics that will cut integration time: 

- SDK versions: redwood-js@2.1.3 or redwood-py==1.8.2 (we will provide a minimal example repo).
- Streaming: use /v1/chat.stream over websocket. Header: Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>, Subprotocol: rw-stream-v1. For quick tests you can use our client helper: new Redwood.StreamClient({url, token}).
- API routes we recommend during trial:
  * POST /v1/text.generate (for batch scoring)
  * WS  /v1/chat.stream  (for low-latency interactions)
  * POST /v1/chat.generate with "function_calls" array for deterministic tool invocation
- Tool calling: provide OpenAPI-style schema for the lookup endpoint; Redwood will map function-calls to your HTTP endpoint during the demo. Expect to send a JSON body and receive structured JSON back — we will validate against the schema in the run.
- KV / caching: enable prefix caching for static catalog queries to reduce token costs; we can add a caching policy in Week 1.
- Quantization/throughput: if you need sustained >10k tokens/sec we should discuss a Dedicated plan; otherwise hosted trial should be fine.

Question for Quantic: will tool endpoints accept requests from Redwood's outbound IPs or do they require a private peering/VPN? If private, we'll need to schedule networking support time.
